land.text: the county, bought in 1421 by Philip the Good: 'Philip became count of Namur on John's death in 1429'

successors.note: The duchy-of-burgundy dossier also records the 1429 gain (counterpart written 'County of Namur'); the page says Philip was also count of Flanders. The county went on as a titled component of the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands until about 1790 ('Under this name it existed from about 990 until about 1790'); the map draws it inside those states, so this dossier ends at 1429.

capitals.name: Namur
capitals.note: The county had its 'military and administrative capital at the town of Namur'.

correction.text: the county of Namur around the town of Namur; the page gives no frontier and no area

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Namur row; the lands sit in its Holy Roman Empire shapes). The page has no infobox or area. The Province of Namur resolves to 4,046 km2, near the 'about 3 k km2' the house-of-luxembourg dossier reads for the county's western lands in 1260 (ratio 1.3). The page says that until the 12th century Namur 'was threatened by its powerful neighbours Brabant, Hainaut and Liège' and that 'important parts of the county were annexed' (Dinant went to Liège), with later compensation, none of it dated, so the shape is a modern-province reading (confidence 2).

correction.text: the county under John I (count of Namur 1305 to 1330), his son and John III, who sold the right to inherit it in 1421

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, the same extent after the Flemish interval (1264-1304, when the lands sit in county-of-flanders). John I page: 'the count of Namur from 1305 to 1330'; the County page: 'In 1421 John III sold the right to inherit Namur to the Duke of Burgundy', who took it on John's death in 1429. No page gives a frontier change.

region.text: the county round the town of Namur

ledger.note: About 990: the County of Namur appears. 'Under this name it existed from about 990 until about 1790'; 'A 986 imperial document refers to a county of Namur', 'An imperial document of 992 calls Albert a count of Namur' and Berengar was called a count of Namur in 919. The page gives no founding date or frontier; the province is the researcher's reading.

1256: Henry V of Luxembourg seizes Namur. 'In 1256, Henry seized Namur while the reigning margrave, Baldwin II, was also reigning emperor in Constantinople'; infobox 'Marquis of Namur 1256-1264'. house-of-luxembourg draws the Namur lands only from its Cliopatria shape of 1260.

1264: Henry V loses Namur. 'Baldwin sold his rights to Namur to Guy, Count of Flanders, who retook the margraviate from Henry'; infobox 'Marquis of Namur 1256-1264; Succeeded by Guy'. The page dates neither the sale nor the retaking; 1264 is the infobox year, and the County of Namur page puts the sale in 1263.

region.text: the county, sold by Baldwin II to Guy of Dampierre

ledger.note: 1264: Guy of Dampierre becomes Marquis of Namur. Guy page: 'Count of Flanders (1251-1305) and Marquis of Namur (1264-1305)'; County of Namur page: 'In 1263 the count of Namur, Baldwin II of Courtenay, sold his county to the count of Flanders, Guy of Dampierre.' The Guy page does not say how he obtained it; county-of-flanders draws only a 25 km disc round Namur for this gain.

region.text: Namur, passing from Guy to John I

ledger.note: 1305: Namur leaves the count of Flanders. John I (son of Guy) 'was the count of Namur from 1305 to 1330'; Guy died on 7 March 1305 (Guy page). Neither page says how or when in 1305 John took the county.

region.text: the county, merged into the Burgundian lands

ledger.note: 1429: Philip the Good takes the county. 'In 1421 John III sold the right to inherit Namur to the Duke of Burgundy, Philip the Good'; 'Philip became count of Namur on John's death in 1429' and 'integrated the county of Namur into a large territorial and political union'. The county survives as a title to about 1790 but is drawn inside the Burgundian state and its Habsburg successors.

wars.name: Henry V of Luxembourg's seizure of Namur

zones.text: Namur, seized by Henry V in 1256 and retaken by Guy of Flanders

wars.outcome: Baldwin II sold his rights to Guy of Flanders, who retook the margraviate from Henry in 1264; Henry and Guy made peace (Guy married Henry's daughter Isabelle).
wars.note: Not a Wikipedia article title: the Henry V page names no war and no battle, only the seizure, the sale and a peace. The ledger treats it as a transfer (loss 1256, gain and loss 1264), not as a contest.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for the county; the Province of Namur is a modern stand-in for the lands of the counts.

notes: Written 2026-11-01 for batch g-eu-b (5 pages opened; budget 2-5). New dossier: Cliopatria has no Namur row. THE STATE: the county of Namur, about 990 to 1429, drawn as the Province of Namur. NOT SETTLED: (1) the dossier ends at 1429 although the County page says the county existed 'until about 1790' as a title; after 1429 the land is drawn by burgundian-state and duchy-of-burgundy (both record a 1429 gain from 'County of Namur', written as a name, not the slug; the two dossiers overlap and the Burgundy group should keep one), then by habsburg-netherlands. (2) 1263 (County page) against 1264 (Guy and Henry V pages) for the sale to Guy; the dossier keeps 1264 to match county-of-flanders and house-of-luxembourg. (3) county-of-flanders draws a 25 km disc round Namur (1,770 km2) for 1264-1305 where this dossier removes the whole province; the remainder falls to nobody's for those years until county-of-flanders is aligned. (4) house-of-luxembourg draws the Namur lands from 1260 only; the Henry V page puts the seizure in 1256. (5) Undated on the pages: the 12th-century losses (Dinant to Liège, parts annexed by Brabant, Hainaut and Liège) and their later compensation; Baldwin V of Hainaut inheriting Namur from Henry the Blind (abdicated 1189; 'The fiefs were dispensed in 1189'; Henry died 1196); Namur under Hainaut's Baldwin V and his successors up to Baldwin II (the Henry the Blind page has no 1188 treaty or 1196 succession war). Open 'Baldwin V, Count of Hainaut', 'Philip I, Marquis of Namur' and 'Namur (city)' to date them. (6) Predecessor left empty: no page opened names Lower Lorraine or Lotharingia as the parent (county-of-namur's land sat in the duchy-of-lower-lorraine on the usual reading). (7) Rulers omitted: no full list opened (pages give Henry the Blind 1139-1189, Henry V 1256-1264, Guy 1264-1305, John I 1305-1330). (8) wikidata null (not read from a page).
